name: Ovation
oneLiner: AI-first guest experience platform built for multi-unit restaurants: two-question SMS surveys, real-time guest recovery, review and listings management, and AI insights from guest feedback.
bestFor: Multi-unit and enterprise restaurant brands that want to catch and fix bad experiences quickly through text-based feedback, and reply to public reviews from the same dashboard.

updates.text: Fall 2025 release added reputation management: reviews from Google, Yelp, Facebook and others, listings across 50+ directories and social in one place, with AI-suggested review replies or templates.
Raised $3 million from nearly a dozen of its own restaurant customers, bringing total funding to $12 million, to expand AI-driven insights and product development.

Spring 2026 release added Brand Voice, tone instructions applied across winback messages, automated responses and review replies, plus a Menu Item Performance Report linking guest sentiment to order data.

features: Two-question SMS surveys sent automatically after orders, through POS and ordering integrations or table QR codes
Real-time alerts on negative feedback so managers can reach out and recover the guest
AI-suggested replies to guest feedback and public reviews, editable before sending, shaped by Brand Voice settings
Review inbox across Google, Yelp, Facebook and more, filterable by platform, rating and location
Listings management across 50+ directories and social posting
AI categorization of written feedback into restaurant-specific themes such as food quality, speed and cleanliness
Competitive Pulse benchmarking against up to five competitors per location
Reports linking guest sentiment to menu items and order data
Integrations with over 50 POS, online ordering and loyalty systems
Operational insights across 35+ feedback categories, with heat maps and custom dashboards
Text marketing and Call-to-Text winback campaigns
Long-form follow-up surveys tied to what guests ordered

pricing.text: Custom pricing; Ovation quotes per account (physical locations and ghost kitchens, with volume discounts) and does not publish prices.

notes: Product is marketed as Ovation at ovationup.com (company sometimes called Ovation Up); founder and CEO Zack Oates. Other 2025 releases: Spring 2025 (April, ROI and long-form survey tools) and Summer 2025 (July, Competitive Pulse and Review Response Visibility), per restaurantnews.com. The Fall 2025 release date (October 15, 2025) comes from search results. Third-party sites (Capterra, GetApp) list a $99/user starting price that does not match Ovation's own custom-quote page; not used. Other brands with case studies on ovationup.com: PDQ Chicken, Earthbar, Big Chicken, VIA 313, Sticky's Finger Joint, Righteous Slice. Nothing in the current review needed dropping; its description matches current positioning. November 2026 check: ovationup.com lists three packages (Retention Marketing, Digital Table Touch, Full CX Suite) with prices hidden and promises a custom quote within 24 hours; no free trial is mentioned. G2's Ovation Up listing showed 4.0 from 2 reviews in a July 2026 snapshot, too few to cite, so no rating key. The 50+ integrations and 35+ categories come from the ovationup.com homepage. The homepage also claims an average 18x feedback increase over long-form surveys (vendor claim, used only qualitatively).
pros: Restaurant-specific: built for multi-unit restaurants, with feedback themes such as food quality, speed and cleanliness
Short SMS surveys: two questions sent automatically after an order through POS and ordering integrations or table QR codes
Fast guest recovery: real-time alerts on negative feedback and AI-suggested replies shaped by Brand Voice
Private feedback, public reviews and listings in one dashboard since the fall 2025 release
Connects with over 50 POS, online ordering and loyalty systems (ovationup.com)
Backed by its own customers: $3 million from nearly a dozen restaurant customers in February 2026

cons.text: No published prices; Ovation gives a custom quote per account after a demo or chat
No free trial is offered on the pricing page or homepage; you schedule a demo
Review and listings management is newer than the survey product: it was added in the fall 2025 release
Few independent reviews: G2 lists only a couple of user reviews, too few to judge it by
Built for restaurants, so groups that also run non-restaurant businesses may need another tool for those

plans.billing: Custom quote per account, counting physical locations and ghost kitchens, with volume discounts
